note.headline: QQQ slips below its 200-day average; SPY holds long trend, breadth thin

summary.thesis: Tech (QQQ) is in a downtrend. It closed at 679.89, just under its 200-day average of 681.20 and well below its 50-day average of 717.72. The broad market (SPY) is moving sideways at 754.37: above its 200-day average of 729.32 but below its 50-day average of 764.09. Fear is normal, but only 27% of stocks are above their 50-day averages.
summary.decision: Long-term: stand aside. Swing: stand aside. The previous note said a QQQ close below its 200-day average would be a stand-aside signal, and that close happened today.
summary.act_at: A QQQ close above 681.20 ends the downtrend, per the market gate. That would support a selective stance again. A QQQ close above 717.72 would put tech's short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's market check.

note.happening: SPY closed at 754.37, down 0.36% from 757.12. QQQ fell further, down 1.2% to 679.89 from 688.17. Over five sessions both are still up: SPY 2.59% and QQQ 3.63%. That is a bounce from the Nov 5 lows of 733.0 for SPY and 647.05 for QQQ. Over 20 sessions both are down: SPY -1.16% and QQQ -4.21%. Both remain below their Oct 6 highest closes of the past year, 779.09 for SPY and 759.66 for QQQ. PPI producer-price data was scheduled for today at 08:30, but DATA contains no result for it and no news since the last note.
note.business: Read together: (1) Trend. SPY's long trend holds, but its short trend is broken. QQQ is below both its 50- and 200-day averages, which counts as a downtrend. (2) Fear. The VIX was about 18.7 on Nov 12, in the 'normal' band (15–20), up from about 17.49 the day before. Its percentile reading is 71 over the past 252 days. The Nov 13 VIX reading isn't stored yet, so this is one day old. (3) Breadth. Only 27% of stocks are above their 50-day averages, so most stocks are in short-term downtrends even though SPY is near its 50-day average. Together: no panic, but tech has lost its long-term trend line and participation is narrow. In general terms (general knowledge), that pattern usually means a few large names are holding up the index.

worth.text: No valuation applies here. The levels below are price-trend markers, not estimates of fair value.
worth.key_assumption: No valuation is implied. The levels are price-trend markers only.

bull: QQQ is only 1.31 (0.19%) below its 200-day average of 681.20, so a small gain would end the downtrend per the market gate.
SPY is 3.3% above its 200-day average of 729.32, so the broad market's long-term trend still counts as up.
Both indices are up over five sessions (SPY 2.59%, QQQ 3.63%) from the Nov 5 lows, which are holding. The VIX is in the normal band, and DATA shows a 5-day change of -9.48.
bear: QQQ closed below its 200-day average of 681.20 and is 5.6% below its 50-day average of 717.72. Its trend is labeled a downtrend.
Breadth is weak: only 27% of stocks are above their 50-day averages.
QQQ fell 1.2% today and is down 4.21% over 20 sessions. SPY is still 1.3% below its 50-day average of 764.09 and 2.5% below its 1-month high of 773.09.

QQQ 50-day average. A close above it would put the short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's market check. That would be the cue to lean in more.
QQQ 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean the tech pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 50-day average. A close above it would put SPY's short-term trend back up.
SPY 1-month high (Oct 21). A close above it would mean SPY's pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 1-month low (Nov 5). A close below it would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline is continuing.
SPY 200-day average. A close below it would put the broad market's long-term trend down too.
QQQ 1-month low (Nov 5). A close below it would mean the tech decline is continuing.

note.headline: Tesla slips to the top of support; valuation still far above cash flow

summary.thesis: Tesla is a grade D business right now: sales are flat, margins are thinner and free cash flow has halved, but the stock still trades near the top of its own 5-year price-to-sales range.
summary.decision: Long-term the call is avoid. On the swing side there is no trade while the price sits between support at 380.15–389.95 and resistance at 393.63–400.51.
summary.act_at: Long-term: revisit near 293.94. Swing: no trade unless the price closes above 417.44 or below 380.15.

note.happening: Tesla closed at 390.22, down 1.82% on the day. That puts it just above the top of its most-tested support zone (380.15–389.95, 10 touches). The 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (385.36, 374.74, 382.73) are all flat, so the stock is moving sideways in a range. There is no news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
note.business: Several numbers point to a real change in the business, not just in mood. Sales in the latest quarter were down 0.17% from a year earlier, after growing 15.78% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, fell to 3.35% from 4.74%. Free cash flow over the last 12 months, the cash left after spending on the business, fell to 3.3B from 6.8B. The filings flag that inventory is up 15% while quarterly sales are up 0%. Unsold cars can force price cuts, which would squeeze the 19.29% gross margin further. These are pressures on demand and margins. The balance sheet is not at risk: Tesla holds 37.5B of net cash (cash minus debt) and 45.4B of total liquidity against 8.0B of debt, so there is no funding problem. The 'tech market in a downtrend' reading from the macro agent affects sentiment, not the business itself.

worth.text: At 390.22, Tesla is valued at about 1542.0B. That is 14.9 times its sales and 429.4 times its earnings per share of 0.91. A cash-flow model (DCF) starts from today's 3.3B of free cash flow and gives 20.23 (bear), 25.02 (base) and 45.34 (bull) per share. Even if growth starts at 30% a year, that model reaches only 44.97. The filings risk note says the price needs about 51% a year growth, while the company delivered 3% a year over 3 years. The second method asks what Tesla is worth if the market keeps paying a price-to-sales multiple in its own 5-year range. That gives 203.8 (low), 293.94 (middle) and 399.81 (high). The gap between the two methods comes from one assumption: whether investors keep paying for future hopes rather than today's cash. The current price-to-sales ratio is at the 78th percentile of its own 5-year history, so the stock sits near the top of the generous method too. (The valuation summary in the data was computed at 397.45, yesterday's price.)
worth.key_assumption: The market keeps valuing Tesla within its own 5-year price-to-sales range rather than on current free cash flow.

bull: Net cash of 37.5B and liquidity of 45.4B mean Tesla can fund its plans through a weak patch without borrowing.
Sales over the last 12 months grew to 103.6B from 95.6B, and analysts' next-year EPS growth is 25%.
The price is above all three of its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (385.36, 374.74, 382.73), and the 380.15–389.95 support zone has held 10 times.
bear: Free cash flow over the last 12 months halved to 3.3B from 6.8B, and operating margin fell to 3.35% from 4.74%.
Inventory is up 15% while latest-quarter sales are up 0%, which can force price cuts.
The base cash-flow value is 25.02 per share against a 390.22 price, and the price implies about 51% a year growth versus 3% delivered over 3 years.

levels.what: Today's close. It is near the top of the history-based range and far above every cash-flow value.
The top of the own-history price-to-sales range. Above it, even the generous method says the stock is expensive.
The middle of the own-history range. At this level the price would no longer need a top-of-range multiple, so it is worth a fresh look if margins stabilize.

longterm.why: Sales are flat while margins and cash flow are falling, and the stock still trades near the top of its own valuation history. The rules committee call is Reduce, and only grade A or B businesses pass the value rules.

swing.why: The price is boxed between support at 380.15–389.95 and resistance at 393.63–400.51. The room to either edge is smaller than the 16.71 average daily range, so a stop would sit inside normal daily noise. A close above 417.44 or below 380.15 would show a direction.

decision.timing: The 2027-01-27 report comes after the 2027-01-15 options expiry, and options price a 14.8% move by then (implied volatility 45.9 vs realized 61.0). That makes the January report the next real test of margins and cash flow, not the coming weeks.

change_mind: At the 2027-01-27 report, quarterly sales growth moving back toward the 15.78% of two quarters ago, with operating margin back above 4.74%.
Free cash flow over the last 12 months recovering toward 6.8B from 3.3B, together with inventory growth falling back in line with sales.
A daily close above 417.44 (top of resistance) would reopen a swing case, and a close below 380.15 would point toward the 364.02–368.6 support.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still avoid long-term and no swing trade. The 1.82% drop to 390.22 moved the stock onto its 380.15–389.95 support, but free cash flow is still shrinking (3.3B vs 6.8B).
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: NVIDIA: leadership turmoil deepens the slide; numbers still strong, earnings decide next

summary.thesis: The business is still growing fast and earning a lot of cash, but the price now assumes about 21.4% starting cash-flow growth while leadership, politics and receivables add risk that the 2026-11-17 report has to address.
summary.decision: Hold the long-term position, don't add before earnings, and make no swing trade until the report is out.
summary.act_at: Hold at 162.85; add near 154.19 only after earnings; reassess near 228.42

note.happening: NVIDIA closed at 162.85, down 2.01% on the day. CNBC reported that the stock is on its longest weekly losing streak since 2012. Media reported Jensen Huang's departure, a Democratic investigation into his dealings with Trump and China, and that the board approached Arm's Rene Haas in its CEO search. Earnings are due on 2026-11-17.
note.business: The things that drive the business have not weakened in the data so far. Revenue over the last twelve months is 303.0B, up from 165.2B. Sales in the latest quarter rose 105.85% from a year earlier, which is faster than the 73.21% of two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 65.21% from 58.09%. Free cash flow is 127.0B, up from 72.0B, and the company holds 23.2B more cash than debt. Most of this week's news is about governance and sentiment: who runs the company and how politicians see it. Some of that can reach the business. Huang's reported role in China relations and in AI financing deals could affect access to China and the terms customers get, though these effects show up in no number yet. Two warnings come straight from the filings. Unpaid customer bills rose 127% while sales rose 106%, which can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly. And a 65% operating margin is the top of its 5-year range of 16–65%, a level that usually fades. Already-reported demand and the cash pile are not at risk. Future margins, receivables quality and the China channel are.

worth.text: On the usual yardsticks the stock looks cheap. It trades at 20.5 times trailing earnings and 10.3 times next year's expected earnings. Its price-to-sales ratio is 13.0, below the peer median of 17.4 and at the 9.0th percentile of its own 5-year history. The cash-flow model (DCF, which values the company on its future cash) gives 195.92 / 228.42 / 272.22 for bear, base and bull. The stock's own price-to-sales history gives 217.35 to 411.04. The gap between methods comes down to one assumption: how fast free cash flow grows from here. At 162.85 the price implies 21.4% starting growth. Holding the discount rate fixed, 20% growth is worth 154.19 and 30% is worth 224.74. Margins matter as much as growth. If operating margin fell to 48%, the value would drop to 115.89, and at 32% it would drop to 77.58. My range is 154.19 to 228.42. The low end is below today's price because the margin peak and receivables warning keep me from fully trusting the higher-growth cases.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing 20–30% a year and operating margin stays near today's 65% instead of falling toward 48%.

bull: Latest-quarter sales growth sped up to 105.85% from 73.21% two quarters earlier, and the operating margin rose to 65.21% from 58.09%.
The stock trades at only 10.3 times next year's expected EPS of 15.85, and that estimate rose 23.6% over 90 days.
Price-to-sales of 13.0 is below the peer median of 17.4 and at the 9.0th percentile of its own 5-year range, while the business keeps quality grade A.
bear: Unpaid customer bills rose 127% against sales growth of 106%, which suggests sales may have been pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly.
A 65% operating margin is the top of the 5-year 16–65% range; at 48% the cash-flow value falls to 115.89.

Leadership is unsettled: the CEO's departure, a political investigation and a CEO search have been reported, insiders sold $946.6M outside pre-set plans, and the stock is in a downtrend below its 50-day average of 214.63.

levels.what: Today's close. It sits inside the fair-value range and implies 21.4% starting cash-flow growth. That supports holding, but leadership is unclear and earnings are four days away, so it does not justify adding.
Value at 20% starting growth, the low end of the range. Add here only after the 2026-11-17 report shows margins near 65% and receivables growing in line with sales.
Base-case DCF value. Near this price the valuation upside is used up, so reassess and consider trimming.

longterm.why: The business numbers and the automated rule ('Buy now') support owning the stock. The committee's 'Hold', the reported leadership upheaval and an earnings report that can gap the price argue against adding now.

swing.why: The stock is in a downtrend with no support level listed below it, and resistance sits just overhead at 163.9–169.14. Earnings fall inside any swing window. Options price a 10.4% move by 2026-11-20, against an ATR (average daily range) of 9.98, so the report can jump past any stop.

decision.timing: Nothing changes before the 2026-11-17 report. Implied volatility of 83.2 against 54.0 realized (1.54x) shows the market is pricing a large move, so act only after the report shows margins, receivables and whether this quarter reached the 108.8B revenue estimate.

change_mind: If the 2026-11-17 report shows operating margin falling back below 58.09% or EPS under the 2.26 low estimate, I would move from hold to trim, because the margin-peak risk would be playing out (value at 48% margin: 115.89).
If the report shows revenue at or above the 108.8B estimate with margin near 65% and receivables no longer growing faster than sales, I would move to add at or below 154.19.
If the stock closes above the 163.9–169.14 resistance zone after earnings, the case for a swing entry reopens, using the 169.91–175.15 zone (5 touches) as the next test.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still hold. The stock fell another 2.01% to 162.85, and reports of a CEO search (Arm's Rene Haas approached) confirm leadership is unsettled with the 2026-11-17 earnings still ahead.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: AMD falls 8.75% to 534.06; business strong, price still above every fair value

summary.thesis: AMD is growing faster and becoming more profitable, but even after today's drop, 534.06 is well above the highest fair value of 333.38.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: wait. The drop broke the prior support zone, and the current support zone is not yet proven.
summary.act_at: Long-term buy at 333.38; swing setup only on a close above 562.99

note.happening: AMD fell 8.75% to close at 534.06, just above the 517.35–530.13 support zone. That reverses yesterday's 5.86% jump to 585.3. The 546.44–562.99 zone that acted as support yesterday now acts as resistance (a price area where selling has tended to cap rallies). Our data has no news since the last note that explains the drop, and the next earnings report is on 2027-02-02.
note.business: Today's fall changes sentiment, not the business. The last filed quarter (filed 2026-11-04) was strong. Sales grew 44.68% from a year earlier, up from 37.85% growth two quarters ago. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 17.72% from 8.78%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) rose to 7.1B from 5.4B over a trailing year. AMD holds 8.7B more cash than debt, so its finances are not at risk. Analysts raised next-year EPS (earnings per share) estimates by 12.1% in 30 days. What is at risk is how long this lasts. Inventory rose 57% while quarterly sales rose 45%, and unsold chips can force price cuts. The filings risk list also notes that an 18% operating margin sits at the top of AMD's 5-year range, and peaks like that usually fade. The macro view is negative, with the tech market in a downtrend. We have no segment data, so we cannot say which product line is driving growth.

worth.text: At 534.06, AMD trades at 116.4 times trailing earnings, 66.1 times this year's expected earnings and 30.2 times next year's. It costs 19.3 times sales, against a peer median of 14.2, and sits in the 95th percentile of its own 5-year price-to-sales range. A discounted cash flow model (today's value of future cash) gives 148.51 to 226.75, with a base case of 190.99. AMD's own price-to-sales history gives 179.24 to 333.38. The price sits above every method. The gap comes from growth. The cash-flow model caps starting growth at 30%, which is worth 187.98, while analysts expect 119% next-year EPS growth. The price assumes that kind of growth lasts for years. Margins matter too: if operating margin falls to 13%, the value drops to 99.12.
worth.key_assumption: The models cap starting growth at 30%, fading over ten years, while the price needs something close to analysts' 119% next-year EPS growth to hold up for much longer.

bull: Sales growth is speeding up: 44.68% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, versus 37.85% two quarters ago.
Profitability roughly doubled: operating margin rose to 17.72% from 8.78%, and free cash flow reached 7.1B.
Analysts keep raising their numbers: next-year EPS is estimated at 17.69, up 12.1% in 30 days, which puts the price at 30.2 times next year's earnings.
bear: Even after the drop, 534.06 is far above the top of the fair-value range at 333.38 and the cash-flow base case of 190.99.
Inventory grew 57% while sales grew 45%, an early warning that could pressure prices and margins; a fall to a 13% operating margin cuts the value to 99.12.
AMD costs 19.3 times sales, against a peer median of 14.2, and sits in the 95th percentile of its own 5-year range, so there is little room for disappointment.

levels.what: Today's close. It is still above every valuation method, so it is not a buy price.
Bottom of the lower support zone (480.33–502.6, tested 5 times). A break below it would signal that the range is failing, but the price would still be above fair value.
Top of the fair-value range (high end of AMD's own price-to-sales history). The valuation case for buying starts here.

longterm.why: The business is improving fast, but the price already assumes the best case. The highest fair value of 333.38 is well below 534.06.

swing.why: Price sits just above the 517.35–530.13 support zone after an 8.75% drop, below the 50-day average of 554.55, and the trend is a range. The nearest resistance at 546.44 is less than one typical daily move (ATR, average daily range) of 41.94 away, so the upside does not justify the risk. A setup would be a close above 562.99 with room up to the 574.2–596.07 zone, or a hold of 480.33–502.6 if 517.35 breaks.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-02-02 are not close yet. Options dated 2026-11-12, priced off 585.3, implied a 16.0% move by 2026-12-18 and 20.1% by 2027-01-15, so large swings like today's should be expected before the report.

change_mind: A close above 562.99 (top of the 546.44–562.99 resistance), with next-year EPS estimates still above 17.69, would support a swing entry.
A close below 480.33 would break the lower support zone and make even a range trade unattractive.
On 2027-02-02, an EPS result below the 3.3 consensus, or inventory again growing faster than sales, would weaken the growth case behind the price.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait on both horizons. The 8.75% fall to 534.06 still leaves price above the 333.38 top of fair value, and it broke the 546.44–562.99 zone that yesterday's swing setup relied on.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: Amazon sits just above its value range while cash burn keeps us waiting

summary.thesis: Amazon's margins are improving, but slower sales growth, heavy cash burn and a price above its own-history value range leave no margin of safety at 266.66.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: no trade while the price sits in the middle of its range.
summary.act_at: Consider buying near 251.93–257.04 support; fuller value at 238.65

note.happening: Amazon closed at 266.66, down 0.29% on the day. That is just above 266.4, the top of its own-history value range. The price has moved sideways, and its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages are all flat. The only news since the last note is a reported discount on a third-party speaker sold on the platform, which has no bearing on the business. No earnings date is in the data.
note.business: Things that change the business: the latest quarter's sales grew 12.09% from a year earlier, down from 16.61% two quarters ago, so growth is slowing. Profitability is improving. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 13.09% from 11.02%. Cash is going the wrong way. Free cash flow, the cash left after spending on the business, was -46.9B over the last 12 months against 10.6B a year before. Debt of 180.9B exceeds cash of 55.8B, leaving net debt of 66.7B, though 114.2B of available liquidity means funding is not under strain. The filings flag unpaid customer bills up 61% while quarterly sales grew 12%. That can mean sales were pulled forward or that customers are paying more slowly. Analysts cut their EPS estimate for next quarter by 2.6% over 30 days, to 2.3. Things that change only sentiment: the speaker headline and the general weakness in tech stocks. The cash position and the margin trend are the real questions. Amazon's ability to stay solvent and its market position (general knowledge) are not at risk.

worth.text: No cash-flow-based valuation (DCF) is possible here because free cash flow is negative. Our only method is Amazon's own history of price-to-sales, which is the share price divided by sales per share. At the 20th, 50th and 80th percentiles of the last 5 years, that gives 187.93, 238.65 and 266.4 per share. The price of 266.66 is just above the top. Price-to-sales is now at the 82nd percentile of Amazon's own 5-year range. The price is 21.6 times trailing earnings and 20.8 times this year's estimate. It is 25.0 times next year's estimate, because analysts expect lower next-year EPS of 10.67 against 12.8 this year. Compared with peers, the stock looks cheaper. Its price-to-sales of 3.6 is below the peer median of 6.6, and on a growth-adjusted basis it trades at 0.62 of peers. That gap explains the difference between the two views: Amazon looks expensive against its own past and cheap against its peers. The filings estimate that the price needs about 34% yearly growth, while Amazon delivered 13% a year over 3 years.
worth.key_assumption: Amazon's price-to-sales stays within its own 5-year range rather than moving toward the peer median of 6.6.

bull: Operating margin improved to 13.09% from 11.02%, so each dollar of sales now produces more profit.
Price-to-sales of 3.6 is well below the peer median of 6.6, and growth-adjusted it trades at 0.62 of peers.
Analysts raised next-year EPS estimates by 1.4% over 30 days and expect revenue of 959.6B next year.
bear: Free cash flow fell to -46.9B over 12 months from 10.6B a year earlier, and net debt stands at 66.7B.
Quarterly sales growth slowed to 12.09% from 16.61% two quarters ago, while the filings estimate the price needs about 34% a year.
The price of 266.66 is above the top of the value range at 266.4, with price-to-sales at its 82nd percentile of the last 5 years.

levels.what: Top of the own-history value range. The price is just above it, so this is not a place to start buying.
Bottom of the strongest support zone (251.93–257.04, 6 touches), where buyers have stepped in before. A reasonable first entry if cash flow stops getting worse.
Midpoint of the own-history value range, where price and fair value meet.

longterm.why: Better margins do not yet outweigh slowing growth and cash burn at a price above the top of the value range. The rule-based verdict is 'Too expensive', and the committee call is 'Reduce'.

swing.why: The price sits inside its current zone of 263.7–267.56. It is between support at 258.08–261.12 and resistance at 274.75–278.56, too close to both for a stop and a target to give good balance. Recent swings (realized volatility 41.7) have also been bigger than options price in (implied volatility 34.3).

decision.timing: No earnings date is in the data. Options to 2026-11-20 price a move of about 4.2%, so the next point to reassess is a test of support at 258.08–261.12 or resistance at 274.75–278.56.

change_mind: Free cash flow over 12 months turns positive again, back toward the 10.6B of a year earlier. That would allow a DCF range and could lift fair value.
Quarterly sales growth reaccelerates back above 16.61%. That would close part of the gap between the roughly 34% a year the price needs and what Amazon delivers.
A daily close below 251.93, the bottom of the strongest support zone, would argue for waiting for 238.65 rather than buying at support.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait, because the 266.66 close remains just above the top of the value range (now 266.4, from 266.17). The committee call moved from 'Avoid' to 'Reduce'.
note.label: Research, not advice.

summary.act_at: add at 486.0–491.22; swing entry only at 504.96–512.76

longterm.why: The business quality is good and the stock is cheap against its history and peers. But estimates are still being cut and the margin is at a peak, so the plan is to buy only at support, where a margin fade to the 59.33 case does less damage.

swing.why: The trend is down: lower highs and lower lows, and price is below three falling averages. There is no trade until the stock either holds 61.15–61.63 or closes above the 20-day average of 64.34 and resistance at 64.84–65.32.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-01-19 come after the 2027-01-15 option expiry, and options price a move of about 11.8% by that date. With estimates still falling, any buying before the report should be small and limited to the support zone.

change_mind: A close below 60.37 (the own-history low), together with another cut to next year's EPS estimate (now 3.77), would mean the selling is about the business, not just sentiment. That would move the decision to avoid until the 2027-01-19 report.
A close above the 66.54–67.49 resistance zone would break the pattern of lower highs and turn the swing view to enter.
If the 2027-01-19 report shows quarterly sales growth below 11.85% and an operating margin below 29.14%, the margin-fade case (59.33 at a 23% margin) becomes the base case.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait for the 61.15–61.63 zone; the 62.15 close is closer to it but still above it, so the buy level has not been reached.
